commenti.body:
Earthlings is a foundational movie for me - I watched it in 2008 and the following day, I became a vegetarian. Now that I can afford to do so, I source my dairy and eggs as ethically as I can. I think documentaries are the best way to expose people to the barbarism of factory farming - most people are already aware of it, but won’t be stirred into further thought or action until they see video of animal torture and suffering for themselves. Disgust is a highly motivating emotion. 

Reading Peter Singer’s Animal Liberation Now is an excellent follow up to further cement the nuts and bolts of the philosophy behind vegetarianism and veganism, and animal welfare as a whole.

Congrats bro! If you want to avoid funding animal exploitation fully when it comes to food, I would ask for you to strongly consider veganism because dairy and eggs also kill animals.

I think Peter Singer's book is good but it's undermined because the man is a speciesist who thinks ethical meat is a thing, he defends bestiality and zoophillia, and is more concerned with welfare than the inherent wrongness of treating sentient beings like they are objects. I would reccomend Tom Regan if you want to read great stuff about a man who is considered by many vegans and activists to be the true father of animal rights.

Also, my post got deleted by the mods, that sucks. I was hoping for a discussion about this film.
